title: skopeo.org is an unaffiliated site presenting as the project home page; this repo sets no canonical URL
body:
## Summary

Googling `skopeo` surfaces <https://skopeo.org>, which presents itself as the project's official home page — nav bar, feature list, "Download Skopeo" button, installation guide, comparison table against Docker and Podman. It is not affiliated with this project. Its own footer says so, in small print below the fold:

> Not affiliated with Skopeo. This is an independent site providing documentation, guides and links to the official project repositories. For official releases visit GitHub

I found it by searching for the tool, not by looking for it, which is the part I think is worth your attention. I searched this tracker and found no prior report.

## What it is

| | |
|---|---|
| Domain registered | 2026-01-29 (Porkbun), expiry 2027-01-29 |
| Hosting | `49.12.122.181` — Hetzner, shared LiteSpeed ("Middlehost"), NS `middlehost.com` |
| Stack | WordPress 7.1 + Astra + Elementor |
| Logo | `cropped-Whisk_f02f215996b5bdc95f849a09a436d1bf...png` — generated with Google's Whisk |
| Outbound links | 31 to itself, 2 to github.com |

The content is machine-generated and was published without review. The "Compatibility Across Systems" section contains four unstripped LLM citation placeholders where the product name should appear:

> 🐧 **Linux Systems** — `:contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}` is optimized for modern Linux environments…
> ☁️ **Cloud Platforms** — `:contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}` integrates seamlessly with cloud-native ecosystems…

(also `oaicite:3` and `oaicite:4`.)

The technical claims are wrong in ways that mislead users:

- The comparison table asserts Docker CLI has no image inspection, and that Podman has "No Advanced Signing ✕" — Podman and Skopeo share the same `containers/image` signing code.
- It states Skopeo is Linux-only, and that installation is "designed for Linux-based environments."
- Its single download link is `github.com/containers/skopeo/archive/refs/heads/main.zip` — a source archive of `main`, offered as the way to obtain the tool.

Its blog mixes three Skopeo articles with football-player biographies (Davinson Sánchez, Bento Krepski) under a single byline, alongside four testimonials attributed to names with no affiliations. This is the standard shape of an SEO domain monetizing a project name.

## Why I'm reporting it rather than ignoring it

To be clear about what this is not: the site is **not** currently distributing a modified binary, and I'm not claiming a compromise. The download link points at genuine GitHub.

What concerns me is the position. This is a name-squatting domain on shared WordPress hosting, ranking on the project's own name, in front of a tool whose entire purpose is moving container images between registries. If that WordPress install is ever compromised — or the domain changes hands — the same page starts handing out an install command to an audience that arrived believing it was official. The gap between "misleading" and "supply-chain problem" is one WordPress plugin CVE wide.

## Suggestions

1. **Set the repo's `homepage` field.** It is currently empty, as is `topics`. Podman and Buildah have podman.io and buildah.io; Skopeo has no canonical site, which is the vacuum this domain filled. Pointing `homepage` at this repo, or at a Skopeo page on podman.io, is a one-field settings change and the strongest canonical signal available here.

2. **A short "Official channels" section near the top of the README**, naming this repository and the distribution packages as the only sources. I'd suggest scoping the ask honestly: this mainly helps people who land in the repo and want to check. I would not expect a README line to change search rankings, and naming the domain in a high-authority page arguably strengthens the association — so it may be better to state what *is* official and not mention the squatter at all.

3. **Report it to Google as spam.** The site fits Google's *scaled content abuse* policy squarely, and the unstripped `oaicite` placeholders plus the unrelated football content are the evidence. I'm happy to file this myself if the project would rather not.

4. **Abuse reports** to Porkbun (`abuse@porkbun.com`) and Hetzner (`abuse@hetzner.com`) — low effort, low odds.

5. **Trademark, if applicable.** Red Hat holds a registered mark on "Podman"; if the same is true for "Skopeo," a UDRP complaint is the only mechanism that actually removes the domain. That's a Red Hat legal call rather than a maintainer one, and I'm raising it here only so it reaches someone who can route it. The footer disclaimer is presumably the intended shield, though a disclaimer below the fold on a domain identical to the mark is generally weak under UDRP.

6. **This probably isn't Skopeo-specific.** The same playbook is cheap to run against Podman and Buildah. If a policy-level answer is wanted, `podman-container-tools/community` may be a better home for it than this tracker.

I can open a PR for (2) — just say which shape you'd prefer, and whether you want
the squatter named or only the official sources listed. (1) needs someone with
write access, since `homepage` is repo metadata rather than a file.
---

*Unrelated, noticed while reading the README:* the release badge and logo still reference `containers/skopeo` (`img.shields.io/github/v/release/containers/skopeo`, `cdn.rawgit.com/containers/skopeo/main/docs/skopeo.svg`) after the org transfer. `rawgit.com` has been shut down since 2019. Happy to fix in the same PR or file separately.
